hints.title: All-Cuts Verification Obstacle
hints.text: Partitioning a string into substrings yields 2^(N-1) possible cut configurations. How can recursive prefix validation avoid exploring deeper cuts when a prefix substring is not palindromic?

hints.title: Valid Prefix Palindrome Invariant
hints.text: Only branch into the remaining suffix if the chosen prefix substring s[start:end] is verified to read identically forwards and backwards.

hints.title: Prefix Bisection Backtracking Procedure
hints.text: At recursion index start: if start reaches len(s), append copy of path to results. Otherwise loop end from start + 1 to len(s) + 1. Check if substring s[start:end] is palindrome. If so, append it to path, recurse with start = end, then pop.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of string s (1 <= N <= 16)
complexity.notes: There are 2^(N-1) potential partitions, with O(N) palindrome checks per candidate cut.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating all partitions blindly before checking palindrome conditions wastes exponential steps.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Path storage takes O(N) memory during recursion.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Early pruning on non-palindromic prefixes and explaining potential DP memoization for palindrome lookups.
